children: barkpark.service is the systemd unit that boots Barkpark via a start.sh which sources ASDF and recompiles deps on boot.
On Production, the running app is the systemd unit barkpark.service. Its ExecStart points at start.sh, which first

— Erlang Solutions ships no ARM packages, so the cax11 box gets its Elixir/Erlang from ASDF, and without it on PATH the boot fails silently. start.sh then recompiles deps on boot before launching the Phoenix API on :4000, behind Caddy.
never skip systemctl restart barkpark after a compile.

The BEAM holds the old code in memory, so a fresh _build/prod does nothing until the process is replaced. This is baked into Deploy — the .githooks/post-merge hook ends in a restart, and make rebuild does the same. The restart is also where the 60–90s cold-boot window lives, while deps recompile and the supervision tree (including the Oban Worker runtime) comes back up.

The service hosts the whole BEAM: Phoenix API, the Oban Worker queues, and the embedded Indx Engine. Because LiveView Studio is rendered inside the Phoenix app, it is served by this same unit — restarting the service is what drops and re-establishes Studio's LiveView socket. A wrong start.sh path once pointed systemd at a file that wasn't there and the process died quietly — the lesson being that the unit and the script must agree. Migration runs out-of-band against the same /opt/barkpark/api with .env sourced, not through this unit.
